PASSO 1: prefixo separável vai para o fi: STEP 1: a separable prefix goes to the end. Be-, ge-, er-, ver-, ent-, emp- stay attached.
English speakers have a head start here: phrasal verbs. "I get up", "I call you back", "the bus pulls in" — English already splits verb and particle. German goes further: the prefix flies to the very END of the sentence, however long it is. «Ich rufe dich morgen um acht Uhr an» — "I call you tomorrow at eight up". Three traps: forgetting to send it to the end, leaving it in the middle (like English "get off at Marienplatz"), and splitting verbs that never split.
Verbos separáveis: o prefixo vai para o: Separable verbs: the prefix goes to the end
Muitos verbos alemães têm um prefixo que: Many German verbs have a prefix that splits off: «aufstehen» (to get up). In the present, the conjugated verb sits in 2nd position and the PREFIX goes to the END of the sentence: «Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf» — like "I get up at seven", but with "up" at the very end. In the infinitive, or with a modal verb, the verb stays whole: «Ich möchte um sieben Uhr aufstehen.» Common separable prefixes: auf- (up), an- (on, at), ein- (in), mit- (with, along), ab- (off, away), fern- (far), aus- (out), zurück- (back) — often the same ideas as English particles. Other prefixes NEVER separate: be-, ge-, er-, ver-, zer-, ent-, emp-: «Ich besuche meine Oma» (besuchen).
em português o verbo não se parte. Em al: English phrasal verbs ("get up", "call back") already split verb and particle, but the particle usually stays close to the verb. In German it goes to the end of the clause, and the whole sentence is "bracketed" between the verb and the prefix.
O prefixo separável vai para o fim da fr: The separable prefix goes to the end of the sentence.

Verbos com a → ä e como dizer quando: Verbs with a → ä, and how to say when
Alguns verbos trocam «a» por «ä» no «du»: Some verbs change «a» to «ä» with «du» and «er / sie / es»: fahren (du fährst), schlafen (du schläfst), laufen (du läufst), waschen (du wäschst), tragen (du trägst). To say WHEN: «um» + clock time (um sieben Uhr — at seven), «am» + part of the day (am Morgen, am Mittag, am Abend — but «in der Nacht», at night), «von … bis» (von neun bis siebzehn Uhr — from nine to five), «jeden Tag» (every day) and the adverbs «morgens, mittags, abends, nachts» for things you do regularly — like English "mornings", "evenings".
Diga: «Morgens trinke ich Kaffee. Um ach: Say: «Morgens trinke ich Kaffee. Um acht Uhr fahre ich zur Arbeit. Abends sehe ich fern. In der Nacht schlafe ich.»
Write 4 sentences with a separable verb.
Two coworkers talk about their routines.
— Quando você se levanta, Jonas?: — When do you get up, Jonas?
— Eu me levanto às seis. E você?: — I get up at six. And you?
— Eu me levanto às sete. Depois tomo ban: — I get up at seven. Then I shower and have breakfast.
— Quando você vai para o trabalho?: — When do you go to work?
— Às oito. Eu trabalho das nove às dezes: — At eight. I work from nine to five.
— E à noite? Você vê televisão?: — And in the evening? Do you watch TV?
— Sim, às vezes. Aí também ligo para os: — Yes, sometimes. Then I also call my parents.
— Eu faço compras à noite com frequência: — I often go shopping in the evening.
— E quando você dorme?: — And when do you go to sleep?
— At ten. I like going to bed early.
Anrufen é separável. Nesta oração declar: Anrufen is separable. In this statement, rufe is the conjugated verb in second position and an goes to the end: Ich rufe dich an.
Der Bus ___ um zehn Uhr ab.
Abfahren é separável. Com der Bus, terce: Abfahren is separable. With der Bus, third person singular, fahren becomes fährt; ab goes to the end of the clause.
Na pergunta de sim/não com mitkommen, o: In a yes/no question with mitkommen, the conjugated verb kommst opens the sentence and mit goes to the end: Kommst du mit?
Einkaufen é separável: Ich kaufe ein. En: Einkaufen is separable: Ich kaufe ein. Of the other options, verstehen and besuchen have inseparable prefixes.
Bekommen has the inseparable prefix be-. It never splits: Ich bekomme ein Buch. Aussteigen and mitnehmen are separable. And careful: bekommen means "to get, receive" — not "to become"!
Depois do modal muss, usa-se o infinitiv: After the modal muss, use the infinitive without zu ("to"). Aufstehen stays whole here: Ich muss früh aufstehen.
Verstehen é inseparável. Com ich, conjug: Verstehen is inseparable. With ich, it's verstehe, keeping ver-: Ich verstehe dich nicht.
